analysis.title: Stocks Are Sensing Greater Downside Risks
key_insights: The VIX rose above 20 in recent days after more than 10 weeks below that level, despite two ongoing wars and concerns over the extent of AI capex.
Simon White's model explains the VIX using the difference between out-of-the-money S&P put skew and call skew, and it fits well.
VIX moves are usually explained by the negative of call skew. Rising call skew, often driven by investors chasing upside, dampens the VIX, and falling call skew lifts it.
This week put skew was the dominant driver, and its rise underpinned the VIX increase more than the decline in call skew did.
The rise in put skew means the implied probability of a market correction has increased, so sentiment may be more fragile than the near all-time highs in the index suggest.
Index correlation is still near its lows, though it has moved a bit higher, and this limits how much rising average single-stock volatility feeds through to the VIX.
Low correlation assumes common-factor risks are muted. A slowdown in AI capex and rising bond yields and volatility are the two counters named.
The author expects further abrupt jumps in the VIX.
risk_factors: A slowdown in AI capex could raise correlation and the VIX.
